title: A local model button on the first-run sign-in screen — the mockups, round 2

steps.path: The screen a new install shows before the app opens
steps.headline: Every way in is now the same outlined button, including Use a local model and Use an API key.
steps.changed: Log in with Claude is no longer filled, Use an API key became a button, and Use a local model was added (your round 1 note, Q-1).
steps.notice: All five buttons look alike and light up on hover. The card is two buttons taller than today.

steps.path: After pressing Use a local model
steps.headline: The card turns into local setup: one model suggested for this computer, then three matching buttons.
steps.changed: Setup happens on this card (Q-2) with one suggestion that fits the computer (Q-3). Download, Choose a different model and Back are all buttons.
steps.notice: Download starts setup and opens the app; Back returns to the five sign-in buttons.
steps.risk: Model names, sizes and the fit line are sample data in this preview.

steps.path: Local setup, after pressing Choose a different model
steps.headline: Choose a different model swaps the suggestion for a list, each model saying how it will run here.
steps.changed: The full recommended list, one row per model, with its download size and whether it fits this computer.
steps.notice: The Download button follows whichever model is picked.

steps.path: Local setup, on a computer with little memory
steps.headline: On a small computer, local setup warns that answers will be slow and suggests signing in instead.
steps.changed: An amber note above the suggestion (Q-6); the option is never hidden.
steps.notice: The suggestion drops to the smallest model and says it will be slow here.

steps.path: The band above the message box, right after setup
steps.headline: While the model downloads, a band above the message box shows its progress and time left.
steps.changed: The app opens straight away (Q-4) and this band stays until the download finishes.
steps.notice: It says plainly that the assistant can answer once the download is done.
steps.risk: The preview shows the band in every chat; built, it appears only in chats using that model.

steps.path: The band above the message box, after quitting mid-download
steps.headline: If setup closed before the download finished, the band says so and offers Resume download.
steps.changed: The app opens normally with this notice (Q-7), instead of reopening setup.
steps.notice: One button picks the download back up where it stopped.

steps.path: After pressing Use an API key and pasting a key
steps.headline: The key box takes any supported key, names whose it is, and Verify & Continue matches the other buttons.
steps.changed: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and OpenRouter keys are recognised from how they start (F-1); the Claude Code sentence is gone (F-2).
steps.notice: Pasting an OpenAI key shows "OpenAI key" before you press Verify & Continue.

steps.path: Pasting a key the app cannot place
steps.headline: A key the app cannot place asks "Which service is this key for?" with a dropdown.
steps.changed: Only an unusual key gets the extra question (F-1).
steps.notice: Verify & Continue stays off until the key is recognised or a service is picked.

steps.path: After pressing Log in with Claude
steps.headline: Log in with Claude installs Claude Code first, on the card, then the browser opens to sign in.
steps.changed: The Claude Code install moved from before this screen to after this click (Q-5, S-1).
steps.notice: Nothing else to press: the sign-in follows on its own once the install finishes.
steps.risk: The install checklist above the card also shows the install, so it is said twice.

steps.path: Settings, Assistant settings, Cloud providers, the Claude Code card
steps.headline: Without Claude Code, its card offers Install Claude Code instead of telling you to restart.
steps.changed: "Restart YouCoded to run setup again" is replaced by an Install button (F-5), since a restart would no longer install it.
steps.notice: One press installs it right here; the card then shows it signed out, ready for the Claude sign-in.

steps.path: The model chip in the bottom strip, a greyed Claude model
steps.headline: Greyed Claude models say "Install Claude Code" and open the card that installs it.
steps.changed: The greyed row's reason becomes a link to the Claude Code card (F-5).
steps.notice: Picking a Claude model without Claude Code is one click away from fixing it.
